final_text:
I changed `Choice.get_metavar` in `src/click/types.py:261`: for options with `show_choices=False`, the metavar is now built from the choices' inferred param type names (via `convert_type(type(choice)).name.upper()`), de-duplicated in first-seen order with `dict.fromkeys` and joined with `|` — so `["foo", "bar"]` → `[TEXT]`, `[1, 2]` → `[INTEGER]`, `["foo", 1]` → `[TEXT|INTEGER]`. Options with `show_choices=True` and all arguments (checked via `param.param_type_name == "option"`) keep the previous value-based metavar, including the `{...}` form for required arguments.

`python -m pytest -q -o pythonpath=src tests/test_options.py` passes (113 passed). Note the repo's current test files contain no `show_choices` metavar tests, so this behavior is not covered by the existing suite.

Bug report for this repository (click):

An option declared with `type=click.Choice([...])` and `show_choices=False` still shows the
choice values in the `--help` metavar, e.g. `-g [foo|bar]`. With `show_choices=False` the
metavar should show the *type names* of the choices instead — the `name` of the param type each
choice value converts to, upper-cased, de-duplicated in first-seen order, joined with `|`:
`[TEXT]` for string choices, `[INTEGER]` for ints, `[FLOAT]`, `[BOOLEAN]`, and `[TEXT|INTEGER]`
for `["foo", 1]`. Options with `show_choices=True` (the default) and arguments keep showing the
values.

Change as little as possible and do not edit the tests. The test command is
`python -m pytest -q -o pythonpath=src tests/test_options.py`; run it once at the end.
